dataset.name: seeded-random-integers
dataset.version: generated from the seed in config.json
dataset.description: Three lists of pseudo-random integers (1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 elements) drawn with Python's random.Random.

findings.statement: On {{metric:largest_size}} random integers the pure-Python merge sort took {{metric:merge_sort_seconds:4}} s and the built-in sorted() {{metric:builtin_seconds:4}} s (medians of 7 repetitions).
Both algorithms returned the same result on every input (results_agree = {{metric:results_agree}}).

limitations: Wall-clock timings on one machine under whatever load it had; they differ between executions and are declared volatile. The ratio of the two times is in metrics.json but is not a declared metric, because the contract compares only durations with a tolerance.
One input distribution (uniform random integers) and three sizes: nothing is shown about sorted, reversed or duplicate-heavy inputs.
The merge sort is a plain textbook version, not a tuned one; the ratio says little about what pure Python could reach.
